title: Gold breaks ₹161,850/10g as dollar strength pressures precious metals lower
summary: MCX gold futures traded near ₹161,853/10g as USD/INR firmed to ₹96.21, offsetting global spot weakness at $4,550/oz. Silver mirrored the move at ₹262,908/kg despite 1.5% intraday volatility. For Indian importers and jewellers, rupee depreciation is cushioning overseas price declines, maintaining local premiums. Copper's stability at $6.35/lb suggests industrial demand resilience. Traders should monitor RBI policy signals and dollar momentum—a break below ₹161,500 in gold could trigger liquidation across bullion contracts.

title: MCX Precious Metals Resume Trading After Four-Hour Technical Disruption Today
summary: MCX gold and silver futures halted for over four hours due to a technical glitch, disrupting intraday liquidity in India's primary bullion contracts. Gold near ₹161,853/10g and silver around ₹262,908/kg faced delayed price discovery, impacting hedging and speculative positioning ahead of global cues. The disruption affects import-linked margins for jewellers and industrialists who rely on MCX settlement for physical hedging and duty calculations. Silver's high volatility during resumption may create arbitrage opportunities against international spot prices, while gold positioning could shift based on overnight global moves. Traders should monitor MCX's investigation timeline and watch for potential circuit-breaker adjustments when markets fully stabilize.

title: Gold, Silver Rally on MCX as Dollar Weakens; Copper Eyes Resistance
summary: Gold surged to ₹161,853/10g on MCX, capitalizing on a weaker rupee at ₹96.21. Silver tracked higher to ₹262,908/kg, benefiting from similar tailwinds. For Indian traders, lower import costs from softening global cues offset by rupee depreciation pressure—a key spread consideration for arbitrage plays. Copper at ₹558-560/kg zone faces technical resistance; watch for breakout signals. Precious metals remain supported by geopolitical uncertainty and portfolio diversification demand. Monitor RBI's next policy stance and global rate-cut expectations for directional cues.

title: Gold slides to ₹1.61 lakh per 10g; silver weakens 1.5% amid dollar strength
summary: Gold futures on MCX have retreated near ₹161,853 per 10 grams as the USD/INR rate holds firm at ₹96.21, making bullion costlier for Indian importers and weakening physical demand. Silver contracts have slipped below ₹262,908 per kilogram, reflecting broader precious metals pressure. For Indian traders, this rupee strength narrows import arbitrage opportunities and pressures margins on forward contracts. The weaker precious metals complex also signals potential demand softness ahead of festive season purchases. Watch RBI policy signals and global DXY momentum for directional cues on rupee stability and metal valuations.

title: Gold crashes 8% below ₹1.34 lakh; silver plunges ₹25,000/kg on global selloff
summary: MCX gold futures have corrected sharply, breaking below the ₹1.34 lakh per 10-gram psychological level amid global deleveraging. Silver has simultaneously fallen ₹25,000/kg, trading near ₹2.63 lakh/kg, reflecting broad precious metals weakness. For Indian importers, lower rupee-denominated prices improve hedging economics despite USD/INR holding at ₹96.21. Jewellers and retailers face margin pressure, though domestic consumption demand may activate on this dip. Copper weakness at $6.35/lb adds deflationary pressure across commodities. Monitor RBI policy signals and global rate expectations for near-term direction; watch if gold stabilizes above ₹1.33 lakh support.

title: Gold Surges Past ₹1.48 Lakh as Dollar Weakens; Silver Rallies 6%
summary: MCX gold futures breached ₹1.48 lakh per 10 grams on weakening USD/INR at ₹96.21, with spot rates near ₹161,853/10g reflecting global bullion strength at $4,550/oz. Silver's 6% jump to ₹262,908/kg signals heightened safe-haven demand amid geopolitical uncertainty. For Indian importers, rupee depreciation increases hedging costs—gold's import duty (12.5%) and GST amplify landed prices for jewelers and industrialists. Silver's volatility impacts fabrication spreads across electronics and silverware sectors. Traders should monitor USD/INR support levels (₹96-96.50) and watch if gold tests ₹1.50 lakh resistance by week-end, alongside Fed rate guidance signals.

title: Gold slips to $4550/oz as USD strength pressures precious metals rally
summary: Gold prices declined to $4550/oz, translating to approximately ₹161,853 per 10 grams on MCX, amid a stronger US dollar at ₹96.21. Silver weakness mirrors this trend at $77.27/oz (₹262,908/kg MCX), pressuring both contracts downward. For Indian importers, rupee strength offers marginal relief on import costs, though precious metals demand typically remains steady during festival season. The 2-3% correction presents tactical opportunities for hedgers managing inventory exposure. Watch for USD/INR movement beyond ₹96.50 and global rate expectations—key triggers for next week's directional momentum.

title: Gold eases to ₹161,853/10g as dollar strength offsets Akshaya Tritiya demand
summary: Gold softened on MCX despite robust festive season demand, pressured by USD/INR strength at ₹96.21. April gold futures likely hover near ₹161,800-₹162,200 range, with import cost competitiveness diminishing as rupee weakens. Silver mirrors the trend around ₹262,900/kg, affecting jewellery and industrial buying decisions. For Indian traders, rupee depreciation offsets global price dips—hedging becomes critical ahead of Akshaya Tritiya peak demand. Copper and crude remain elevated, straining downstream industries. Watch RBI commentary and gold import data for directional cues this week.

title: ** Gold slides ₹161,677/10g as global correction weighs on MCX sentiment
summary: ** Gold tumbled sharply across MCX after breaking its record highs, with spot prices falling approximately 5% to ₹161,677/10g levels. Silver mirrored the decline, pressuring ₹262,020/kg contract as profit-taking dominates. For Indian traders, the correction eases import duty calculations on bullion inflows while narrowing hedging spreads against physical inventory. Weaker precious metals may attract fresh accumulation from jewellers ahead of festival demand. Watch for USD/INR stability at ₹96.21 and upcoming US inflation data—any dovish signals could reignite precious metal demand.

title: Gold, Silver Plunge 11% on MCX; Precious Metals Turn Negative for 2026
summary: Gold and silver contracts on MCX have declined over 11% amid extended global sell-off, with bullion now posting negative returns for 2026. Gold trades near ₹161,677/10g while silver hovers around ₹262,020/kg—both pressured by dollar strength (USD/INR at ₹96.21) and cooling safe-haven demand. For Indian importers and jewellers, lower rupee conversion costs present tactical opportunities, though import duty structures remain unchanged. The sharp correction raises inventory valuation concerns for traders holding long positions. Watch for fresh technical support levels and global inflation data releases, which may signal whether the downtrend consolidates or reverses.

title: Gold hits $4545/oz as rupee steadies; MCX positioning shifts on dollar strength
summary: Gold prices climbed to $4545/oz, translating to approximately ₹161,677 per 10g on MCX as safe-haven demand resurfaces amid geopolitical concerns. MCX gold contracts face resistance near ₹162,000 levels; a break above signals renewed institutional accumulation. Silver at $77.01/oz (~₹262,020/kg) trails precious metals strength, creating a widening gold-silver ratio that pressures spreads for multi-metal portfolios. For Indian importers, the stable INR at ₹96.21 offsets some upside, but import duty calculations remain sensitive to spot volatility. WTI crude's resilience at $98.15/bbl supports energy hedging demand. Watch for US inflation data this week and any Fed commentary signaling rate trajectory shifts.

title: ** Gold slides to $4545, silver crashes below $77—MCX precious metals weaken on dollar strength
summary: ** Gold dropped to $4545/oz while silver crashed below $77/oz, translating to MCX Gold near ₹161,677/10g and MCX Silver around ₹262,020/kg. The sharp decline reflects USD/INR strength at ₹96.21, pressuring rupee-denominated precious metals despite stable import duty structures. For Indian jewelers and traders, lower MCX prices reduce hedging costs but signal margin compression in retail positioning. Silver's steeper fall raises concerns for industrial users reliant on forward contracts. Watch for USD/INR movement above ₹96.50 and Fed commentary—potential triggers for further precious metals volatility.

title: ** Gold breaks 4-week rally above ₹161,677; silver plunges 6% amid USD strength
summary: ** Gold spot prices have breached $4,545/oz as USD/INR strengthens to ₹96.21, signaling potential downside for MCX Gold futures from current ₹161,677/10g levels. Silver's 6% decline to $77.01/oz pressures MCX Silver toward ₹262,020/kg, with both precious metals vulnerable to further rupee depreciation. For Indian traders, stronger dollar imports increase hedging costs and widen gold-silver spreads; margin requirements on leveraged positions may tighten. The downturn reflects global risk-off sentiment and elevated US rates. Watch US inflation data and Fed policy signals for reversal triggers at ₹160,500 (gold) and ₹258,000 (silver) support levels.

title: ** Gold and silver surge 7% on MCX as India hikes bullion import duties
summary: ** Gold and silver futures rallied over 7% on MCX following India's import duty increase on bullion. Gold MCX hovered near ₹161,677/10g while silver traded around ₹262,020/kg, reflecting stronger INR positioning and duty-driven arbitrage opportunities. The duty hike raises import costs for refiners and jewellers, supporting domestic contract premiums against global benchmarks. This narrows traditional import spreads, potentially redirecting physical demand toward MCX contracts. Traders should monitor duty implementation timelines and track whether the ₹161,677 gold level holds as fresh resistance or support.
